name: Al Pastor Pork Taco Bowl with Cilantro Lime Rice
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 7 tbsp (105 g)
Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 5 tbsp (84 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 2.3 cans (595 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 8.75 oz (250 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Blend the marinade: orange juice, achiote paste, chipotles in adobo, apple cider vinegar, garlic, half the onion, brown sugar, cumin, oregano, salt, pepper, and about half the olive oil. Blend until smooth.
Slice the pork loin into thin strips, toss with the marinade, and let it sit at least 30 minutes in the fridge (overnight is better).
Start the rice: cook 3.5 cups dry rice with water per package directions, then stir in a squeeze of the pineapple juice at the end.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear the pork in batches so it browns instead of steams, about 4 to 5 minutes per batch, until cooked through to 145F with no pink.

Push the pork aside, add the drained pineapple chunks and remaining onion, and let them char for 3 to 4 minutes. Toss everything together with any leftover marinade and simmer 2 minutes until it coats the meat.
Warm the seasoned black beans in a small pot.
Combine the rice, pork, pineapple, and beans in your big pot, then top each portion with a sprinkle of the Mexican cheese blend when you pack the containers.

name: Albondigas en Chipotle (Mexican Meatballs in Chipotle Sauce)
ingredients: Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 4 tbsp (66 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Tear the sandwich bread into pieces, soak it in the milk until soft, then mash it into a paste.
Mix the ground beef with the bread paste, eggs, some of the garlic, salt, and black pepper, and roll it into evenly sized meatballs.
Blend the diced tomatoes with the chipotles in adobo, the yellow onion, and the rest of the garlic into a smooth sauce.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot and pour in the blended sauce carefully, since it will spit. Cook it down for several minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Add the chicken broth, bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, and lower the raw meatballs in one by one.
Cover and simmer gently, without stirring for the first fifteen minutes so the meatballs set, until they are cooked through.
Cook the rice according to the package, then finish the pot with the chopped cilantro and adjust the salt.

name: American Goulash Pasta
steps: Brown 5.4 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion and shredded carrots, then drain.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, garlic, and italian seasoning.
Boil the penne separately until just tender, then drain.
Simmer the sauce a few minutes so it thickens, then fold in the cooked pasta.
Stir in the parmesan and portion it into containers.

name: Andong Jjimdak (Korean Soy-Braised Chicken with Noodles)
ingredients: Korean glass noodles (dangmyeon): 14 oz dry (397 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.75 lb (3033 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4 tbsp (70 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the Korean glass noodles (dangmyeon) in cold water for 30 minutes while everything else cooks. Do not boil them yet.
Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and blanch them in boiling water for two minutes, then drain and rinse. This gives you a clean braising liquid rather than a murky one.
Whisk the soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, honey, garlic, ginger, black pepper, and a spoonful of cocoa powder together. The cocoa is what gives jjimdak its dark color without turning it bitter.
Put the chicken in a wide pot with the sauce and enough water to come halfway up, add the dried arbol chiles, and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrots, and onion in big chunks and cook another 20 minutes until they are tender and the liquid has reduced by about a third.
Drain the soaked noodles, add them to the pot with the sliced jalapeno, and cook 5 more minutes until they turn clear and springy. They will drink up a lot of the sauce, which is the point.
Taste for salt and sweetness, then pull it off the heat before the noodles go soft.

name: Ants Climbing a Tree Pork Noodles
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 28 oz dry (794 g)
Doubanjiang (Lee Kum Kee (Chili Bean Sauce Toban Djan)): 4 oz (112 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice noodles in warm water until pliable but not soft, then drain and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the ginger for about thirty seconds, until it smells sharp.
Stir in the doubanjiang and cook it in the oil for another minute so the paste turns deep red and loses its raw edge.
Add the ground pork, break it up, and cook until no pink remains.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and sugar, and bring it up to a simmer.
Add the drained noodles, turn the heat to low, and simmer uncovered until the noodles are tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
Kill the heat, fold in the green onions, and season with salt and black pepper to taste.

name: Apple Cider Beef Pot Roast Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it with salt, black pepper, thyme, and Italian seasoning, and sear it in the vegetable oil until browned on all sides.
Move the roast to the slow cooker. Whisk the apple juice, beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, tomato paste, Dijon mustard, and minced garlic together.
Pour that liquid over the roast, scraping any browned bits from the searing pan in with it.
Cut the carrots and potatoes into large chunks so they survive the full cook, and tuck them around the roast.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef gives with no resistance and the vegetables are soft through.
Lift the roast out, shred it, and return it to the pot with the vegetables.
Taste the liquid. If it reads too sweet, a splash more Dijon or a pinch of salt will square it up.

name: Arroz con Carne Molida (Mexican Beef and Rice Skillet)
ingredients: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2.3 cans (1008 g)
Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 2.3 cans (660 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 28 oz (793 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground beef in your largest skillet or pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains (ground beef should hit 160F). Drain excess fat.
Stir in the taco seasoning, diced onion, minced jalapeno, and garlic. Cook 3 to 4 minutes until the onion softens.
Add the dry rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes so it toasts lightly in the beef drippings.

Pour in the diced tomatoes with green chilies, the corn with its liquid, and enough water to cook the rice (about 2 cups of water per cup of dry rice, minus the can liquid). Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to a low simmer for 18 to 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Stir once halfway so nothing sticks.
Kill the heat, scatter the Mexican cheese blend over the top, and cover for 3 to 4 minutes until it melts into the rice.

name: Arroz con Pollo (Chicken and Rice) Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and cumin. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high and brown the thighs in batches, about 3 minutes per side. Set them aside; they finish cooking later.
In the same pot, cook the diced onion and green bell pepper for 4 to 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in the dry rice, tomato paste, oregano, turmeric, sugar, and bay leaves. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring, so the rice takes on color and flavor.
Pour in the chicken broth, scrape up the browned bits, and nestle the thighs back in along with any juices.
Bring to a boil, cover, and drop to a low simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165F.
Turn off the heat, scatter the olives and frozen peas over the top, and re-cover for 5 minutes. The residual heat warms them without turning the peas to mush.
Pull the bay leaves, shred or chop the chicken into bite-size pieces, stir everything together, and finish with the chopped cilantro.

name: Asado de Puerco (Mexican Red Chile Pork Stew) Bowls
ingredients: Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 5 cans (1441 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork loin into bite-sized cubes and pat them dry, then season with salt, ground cumin and black pepper.
Sear the pork in the olive oil in a heavy pot over high heat, in batches, until the pieces are browned on at least two sides. Crowding the pan is the one mistake to avoid here.
Drop the heat, add the minced garlic, and stir for a minute until it smells sweet.
Pour in the enchilada sauce and the tomato sauce, scrape the bottom of the pot clean, and bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for about 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is tender and the sauce has thickened and darkened.
Cook the rice per the package while the pork simmers, and taste the sauce for salt at the end.

name: Asian Ground Pork Meatball Rice Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.5 tbsp (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Preheat the oven to 400F and line two sheet pans. In a big bowl, mix the ground pork with the grated onion, most of the garlic, the ginger, soy sauce, bread crumbs, half the cilantro, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper. Do not overwork it.
Roll the mixture into golf-ball-size meatballs (you should get 40 to 45) and space them out on the sheet pans.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes until browned and cooked through; ground pork needs to hit 160F in the center.

While they bake, make the coconut rice: combine the dry rice, both cans of coconut milk, and enough water to hit your usual rice ratio. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer low 18 to 20 minutes, then rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Whisk the drizzle: lime juice, sriracha, rice vinegar, and the remaining garlic.
Combine the rice and meatballs in your big pot, pour the drizzle over, and toss gently so the meatballs stay whole. Finish with green onions and the rest of the cilantro.

name: Baked Sausage and Egg Breakfast Hash
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.5 lb (280 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Dice the potatoes small, chop the red bell pepper and red onion, and chop the bacon.

Toss the potatoes with the olive oil, smoked paprika, dried thyme, onion powder, garlic powder, salt and black pepper, then spread them across two large sheet pans and roast until they start to crisp.
While they roast, cook the chopped bacon and the ground pork in a skillet, breaking the pork into crumbles, until both are browned and the fat has rendered.
Add the pepper and onion to that skillet and cook until they soften in the sausage fat.
Scatter the sausage mixture over the roasted potatoes and toss it together on the pans.
Make wells in the hash with the back of a spoon and crack the eggs into them. A well is not optional here, because eggs cracked onto a flat surface run everywhere.
Return the pans to the oven and bake just until the whites set and the yolks are still soft, then combine everything gently in your big pot.

name: Baked Sweet and Sour Chicken Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 4 lb (1867 g)
Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 0.5 cups (140 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 325F. Cut the chicken breast into bite-size cubes and season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Set up a dredge: cornstarch in one bowl, beaten eggs in another. Toss the chicken in cornstarch, then coat in egg.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Brown the chicken in batches, 1 to 2 minutes per side; it just needs color, not doneness yet. Move it to one or two 9x13 baking dishes.
Whisk the sauce: sugar, ketchup, white vinegar, apple cider vinegar, and soy sauce. Pour it evenly over the chicken.
Bake for about 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes so the sauce thickens and glazes every piece. Chicken is done at 165F.
While it bakes, cook the rice with water per package directions.
Combine the rice and glazed chicken in your big pot, scraping every bit of sauce out of the baking dishes.

name: Baked Turkey Kibbeh Casserole
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cover the bulgur with cold water and let it soak 20 to 30 minutes until the grains soften, then drain it and squeeze out every bit of excess water with your hands.
Set aside about a third of the ground turkey and a third of the onions for the filling, then finely mince the remaining onions for the shell.

Mix the soaked bulgur with two thirds of the ground turkey, the minced onion, the ground allspice, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper, kneading it with wet hands until it turns into a smooth, almost paste-like dough.

For the filling, heat some of the olive oil in a skillet and brown the reserved turkey with the reserved diced onion, seasoning it with more allspice, salt, and black pepper, then stir in the chopped fresh basil off the heat.
Press half the bulgur mixture into an oiled 9x13 pan in an even layer, spread the filling over it, then press the remaining bulgur mixture on top, smoothing it with wet hands.
Score the top into diamonds with a wet knife, cutting through the top layer only, then drizzle the rest of the olive oil generously over the whole surface.
Bake at 375F for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is deep golden and the edges pull away from the pan, then rest 15 minutes before portioning.

name: Baked Ziti with Ground Beef
ingredients: Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 28 oz dry (794 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 9.25 oz (264 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 375F. Boil the ziti in salted water until just shy of al dente, about 2 minutes under the package time. Drain.

While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground beef with the diced onion, breaking it up as it goes, until no pink remains (160F for ground beef). Add the garlic for the last minute, then stir in the marinara, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, eggs, half the Parmesan, salt, and pepper.
In two 9x13 pans, layer: a third of the meat sauce, half the pasta, half the ricotta mixture in spoonfuls, then repeat, finishing with sauce on top.
Top with the mozzarella and remaining Parmesan. Bake 25 to 30 minutes until bubbly and browned at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes before combining into your weighed pot; it holds together better and will not steam-soften in the containers.

name: Baked Ziti with Ground Turkey and Ricotta
ingredients: Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 37.25 oz dry (1058 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 18.5 oz (527 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 375F. Boil the ziti in salted water until just shy of al dente, then drain.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high and brown the ground turkey with the minced garlic, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains; ground turkey should reach 165F. Season well with salt and pepper.
Pour in the marinara sauce and simmer 5 minutes so the turkey soaks up the tomato flavor.
Fold in the drained ziti, most of the chopped fresh basil, and half the mozzarella until everything is coated in sauce.
Spread into two 9x13 pans, dollop the ricotta over the top in big spoonfuls, then finish with the remaining mozzarella and the Parmesan. Bake 20 to 25 minutes until melted and golden at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes, scatter the last of the basil over the top, then combine into your weighed pot for portioning.

name: Slow Cooker Balsamic Beef Pot Roast Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry and season it hard with salt, black pepper, oregano, and basil.
Sear it in the vegetable oil over high heat until it is browned on every side, then move it to the slow cooker.
Chop the onion and mince the garlic and scatter them over and around the roast.
Whisk the balsamic vinegar with the olive oil and pour it over the top.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the roast falls apart under a fork.
Shred the beef in the cooker and stir it through the balsamic gravy, letting it sit 10 minutes so the meat drinks some back up.
Cook the rice separately and keep it plain so the vinegar has something to land on.

name: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Peel and chunk the potatoes and get them going in salted water. Slice the onions thin and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet and brown the sausages slowly on all sides. Low and slow keeps the casings from splitting.
Move the sausages to a plate and start the gravy in the same pan, melting most of the butter and cooking the sliced onions until they go deep golden and sweet.
Add the garlic, then sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute before streaming in the chicken broth while whisking.
Add the soy sauce and simmer the gravy until it thickens and coats a spoon, then season with salt and black pepper.
Drain the potatoes, mash them with the remaining butter, salt and pepper, and keep them loose enough to portion easily.
Warm the peas through, slice the sausages into thick coins, and combine everything with the gravy in your big pot.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Season the pork shoulder with salt, black pepper and smoked paprika, sear it in the vegetable oil, then slow cook it with the minced garlic, the diced onion and the bay leaves for 8 to 9 hours on low.
Scrub the sweet potatoes, prick them all over with a fork, and roast at 400F for about an hour until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Pull the pork apart with two forks and skim the fat off the cooking liquid.
Toss the shredded pork with the barbecue sauce and a few spoonfuls of the skimmed cooking liquid so it stays moist rather than pasty.
Split each roasted sweet potato lengthwise and press the flesh open with a fork to make room.
Fill each one with the barbecue pork and keep the sour cream, diced onion and chopped cilantro in separate containers to add at reheat.

name: Beef Birria Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stem and seed the guajillo, ancho, and arbol chiles, then toast them in a dry pan about 30 seconds a side until they smell fragrant. Do not let them blacken or the sauce turns bitter.
Cover the toasted chiles with hot water and soak 20 minutes until they are soft and pliable.
Blend the drained chiles with the diced tomatoes, onion, garlic, white vinegar, cumin, oregano, cinnamon, and cloves until completely smooth. Strain it if you want a silkier consomme.
Cut the chuck roast into large chunks, season with salt and black pepper, and sear them in the olive oil until browned.
Pour the chile sauce and the beef broth over the beef, add the bay leaves, and bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook 3.5 to 4 hours on the lowest heat that keeps it moving, until the beef falls apart when pushed.
Shred the beef and return it to the consomme, then taste and correct the salt and the vinegar.

name: Beef Bourguignon Bowls
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 1 lb (420 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it in the pot until crisp. Lift it out and leave the fat.
Cut the chuck into large cubes, dry them well, season with salt and black pepper, and brown them hard in the bacon fat and vegetable oil in batches.
Slice the onions and cook them in the same pot, patiently, until they are soft and deeply golden. This takes a while and it is where the sweetness comes from.
Add the garlic, then stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, scraping the bottom clean, and add the bay leaves and thyme.
Return the beef and bacon, cover, and simmer very low for 2.5 hours, until the beef breaks apart under a spoon.
Saute the sliced mushrooms and the carrots in the butter in a separate pan until browned, then stir them in for the last 20 minutes so they keep their shape.

name: Beef Bulgogi Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Grate the apple and the onion into a bowl and whisk in the soy sauce, sesame oil, mirin, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and black pepper. That is your bulgogi marinade and it should smell sweet, salty, and toasty all at once.
Toss about two thirds of the marinade through the thin-sliced beef and let it sit at least 30 minutes in the fridge. Hold the rest back for finishing.
Start the rice so it is ready when the beef is.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high and sear the beef in two batches, spread out in a single layer. Let each batch sit undisturbed for a minute at a time so it browns instead of steaming. Browning is where the caramel notes come from.
Pour the reserved marinade into the skillet with all the beef and let it bubble down for 2 to 3 minutes until it glazes the meat.
Warm the frozen spinach and the shredded carrots briefly in a separate pan so they keep their color, then season lightly with salt.
Sprinkle the toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions over everything just before packing.

name: Beef Chili Mac
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (160 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain.
Stir in the kidney beans, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth, chili powder, cumin, and garlic.
Simmer until the chili thickens and the flavors come together.
Boil the penne separately until just tender, then drain and fold it in.
Melt the shredded cheddar over the top before portioning into containers.

name: Beef Chow Mein Noodles
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 49.5 oz dry (1400 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 6.75 oz (189 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the lo mein noodles 1 minute short of package directions, drain, rinse briefly with cool water, and toss with a splash of the oil so they do not clump.
Whisk the sauce: soy sauce, oyster sauce, chicken broth, sugar, and flour. Set it by the stove.
Heat a little oil in your largest skillet or wok over high heat. Scramble the beaten eggs into ribbons, then set them aside.
Add more oil and brown the ground beef with the garlic, breaking it up, until no pink remains; ground beef should hit 160F. Season with salt and pepper.
Pile in the shredded cabbage and carrots and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes until they wilt but keep a little crunch.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens, then add the noodles, eggs, and green onions and toss until everything is glossy and coated.

name: Beef Enchilada Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 8 cans (3066 g)
Enchilada Sauce (Old El Paso): 3 cans (600 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (500 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (224 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
Corn Tortillas: 5, cut into triangles (440 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, then drain off the grease.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin and let them bloom in the hot beef for a minute.
Add the enchilada sauce and corn and simmer until it thickens up a bit.
Fold in the seasoned black beans and warm everything through.
Spoon it into bowls over the beans, then top with shredded cheddar so it melts in.

name: Chinese Beef with Honey Black Pepper Sauce
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 5.25 tbsp (94 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain, then toss it with cornstarch and a splash of the soy sauce until every piece is lightly coated. Let it sit 15 minutes.
Start the rice.

Whisk the honey, oyster sauce, mirin, remaining soy sauce, and a heavy amount of coarse black pepper into a cup. Taste it. It should be aggressively sweet and aggressively peppery, because the beef and rice will tone it down.
Get a large skillet ripping hot and sear the beef in batches without moving it for the first minute. Pull each batch out just short of done.
Add the sliced onion to the pan and cook 2 to 3 minutes until it softens at the edges, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble hard until it thickens and turns glossy, which takes about a minute. Watch it closely, because honey sauces go from perfect to scorched fast.
Return the beef with its juices, toss to coat, and scatter the chopped peanuts over the top just before packing so they stay crunchy.

name: Beef Keema Curry Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Start the rice: cook 6.5 cups dry rice with water per package directions while you make the keema.
Heat the olive oil in your largest pot over medium heat. Cook the diced onions 6 to 8 minutes until golden at the edges, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute more.
Add the ground beef, turn the heat to medium-high, and brown it thoroughly, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains; ground beef should reach 160F.
Stir in the curry powder, cumin, turmeric, salt, and pepper and toast the spices in the fat for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and a splash of water, then simmer 10 minutes so the flavors marry and the mixture thickens.
Stir in the frozen peas for the last 3 minutes, then kill the heat and fold in most of the chopped cilantro.
Combine the rice and keema in your weighed pot and top with the remaining cilantro.

name: Beef Manhattan Bowls
ingredients: Brown Gravy Mix (generic dry (USDA)): 2.25 oz (66 g)
Onion Soup Mix (Great Value): 2.25 oz (66 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it with salt and black pepper, and sear it in the olive oil until it is browned on every side.
Set the roast in the slow cooker and sprinkle the brown gravy mix and onion soup mix over the top.
Add the red wine vinegar and enough water to come about a third of the way up the roast.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef shreds with no effort.
About 40 minutes before you portion, peel and boil the potatoes until a knife slides through, then drain and mash them with some of the hot gravy from the cooker.
Shred the beef in the cooker and stir it through the gravy so nothing dries out.
Taste the gravy. Two seasoning packets bring plenty of salt, so it likely needs pepper rather than more salt.

name: Beef and Mushroom Stir-Fry Rice Plate
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.5 cups (168 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain and toss it with most of the cornstarch, a pinch of baking soda, some soy sauce, and a splash of water, then let it sit for at least fifteen minutes.
Cook the rice according to the package while the beef rests.
Stir the remaining cornstarch into a little cold water and mix it with the oyster sauce, the rest of the soy sauce, the beef broth, the chicken broth, sugar, and black pepper to make the sauce.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok until it smokes and sear the beef in batches in a single layer, just until browned, then set it aside. Do not cook it through, since it will finish in the sauce.
Add the butter to the pan and cook the mushrooms hard, without stirring much, until they release their water, it cooks off, and they brown.
Add the ginger, garlic, and the white parts of the green onions and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce mixture, bring it to a boil until it thickens and turns glossy, return the beef, add the sesame oil and the green onion tops, and toss to coat.

name: Cuban Beef Picadillo Rice Bowls
ingredients: Salt (Morton): 1/8 to 1/2 tsp fine salt (6 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, green pepper, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, olives, and golden raisins.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes so the flavors come together.
Cook the rice while the picadillo simmers.
Spoon the beef over rice and serve.

name: Slow Cooker Beef and Potato Au Gratin Casserole
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 28 oz (791 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet with the paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until no pink remains, then drain the fat.
Peel the potatoes and slice them thin and even, about an eighth of an inch. A mandoline is fastest, a steady hand and a sharp knife works.
Slice the onion thin as well.
Layer half the potatoes in the slow cooker, then half the onion, half the beef, and a third of the cheddar. Repeat the layers.
Pour the chicken broth over the top and finish with the last of the cheddar.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, until a knife goes through the potatoes with no resistance.
Turn the cooker off and let it sit uncovered 15 minutes so the layers set enough to lift out cleanly.

name: Simple Beef Ragu Pasta
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, carrots, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, and Italian seasoning.
Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and rich.
Cook the penne until just tender, then toss it with the sauce.
Finish with a shower of parmesan over the top.

name: Beef Rendang Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Blend the onion, garlic, ginger, and jalapeno into a rough paste. Add a splash of water if the blender needs help moving.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wide heavy pot and fry the paste over medium heat until it darkens and smells sweet rather than raw, about 10 minutes. This is the single most important step, so do not shortcut it.
Stir in the lemongrass paste, turmeric, cinnamon, bay leaves, and black pepper and cook another minute.
Add the beef cut into large cubes and turn it in the paste until every piece is coated.
Pour in the coconut milk with the brown sugar and salt, bring it to a simmer, and cook uncovered on low for 2 to 3 hours. Stir every 20 minutes or so, more often near the end.

Keep going past the point where it looks done. The liquid will reduce, then break, then the beef starts frying in the coconut oil that separates out and everything turns deep brown. That is rendang, and it is a different dish from the milky stew it was an hour earlier.
Taste for salt and pull it off the heat while there is still a little gloss on the meat.

name: Middle Eastern Beef, Spinach and Chickpea Stew
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the diced yellow onion until softened and lightly golden.
Add the ground beef, break it up, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook it for a couple of minutes until it darkens and coats everything, which takes the tinny edge off.
Thaw the frozen chopped spinach, squeeze out most of the water, and add it to the pot.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered until the spinach has melted into the sauce and the stew thickens.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, add them, and simmer another ten minutes so they take on the sauce.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste, then cook the rice according to the package to serve underneath.

name: Beef Stuffed Shells
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 19.5 oz dry (556 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 23.25 oz (659 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 375F. Boil the pasta shells in salted water until just flexible, about 2 minutes shy of the package time, then drain and lay them out so they do not stick together.

Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high and brown the ground beef with the diced onion until no pink remains (160F for ground beef). Add the garlic for the last minute, then stir in the marinara and tomato paste and simmer 5 minutes.
Make the filling: mix the ricotta, eggs, Parmesan, about a third of the mozzarella, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Spread a layer of meat sauce across the bottom of two 9x13 pans. Spoon the filling into the shells and nestle them in, open side up.
Pour the remaining meat sauce over the shells and top with the rest of the mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 more until the cheese is bubbly and starting to brown. Rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Slow Cooker Beef Tips and Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes, pat them dry, and season with salt, black pepper, and paprika.
Sear the cubes in the olive oil in batches over high heat until they have real color, then move them to the slow cooker.
Cook the chopped onion and minced garlic in the same pan until soft, scraping up every browned bit, then add them to the cooker.
Pour in the beef broth along with the Worcestershire sauce and Dijon mustard from the pantry list.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours, until the beef cubes give with no resistance.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little cold water, stir it into the hot liquid, and cook on high 15 to 20 minutes until the gravy thickens and turns glossy.
Cook the rice separately and spoon the beef tips and gravy over it. In a diner it would be mashed potatoes, and if you keep potatoes on hand that works too.

name: Beijing Zha Jiang Mian Pork Noodles
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 35.25 oz dry (998 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the pork shoulder small, roughly pea-sized, so it eats like a sauce rather than a stew.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and cook the pork over medium-high heat until it browns and renders its fat.
Add the garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the green onions and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the hoisin sauce and soy sauce and let them fry in the fat for a minute, which is what takes the raw edge off.
Pour in the chicken broth, drop the heat to low, and simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and glossy and the pork is tender.
Boil the lo mein noodles to just tender, drain, and rinse briefly so they do not clump.
Cut the cucumber and carrots into matchsticks, then serve the sauce over the noodles with the raw vegetables and the green onion tops piled on.

name: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 1.5 lb (700 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Drain the sauerkraut but do not rinse all the tang out of it. Core and shred the fresh cabbage, dice the onions, and slice the mushrooms.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot and brown the chicken thighs and the sliced smoked sausage until both have real color on them. Take them out and set them aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot until soft, then add the mushrooms and let them give up their water.
Stir in the sauerkraut, the shredded cabbage, the tomato sauce, the caraway seeds and the bay leaves.
Return the meat, add enough water to keep everything just submerged, and bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and cook low and slow for a couple of hours, stirring now and then. This is a stew that rewards patience, not heat.
Stir in the golden raisins near the end, season with salt and black pepper, and cook the rice separately to serve it over.

name: Bistek Tagalog (Filipino Beef and Onions over Rice)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the beef thin against the grain. Toss it with the lemon juice, soy sauce, minced garlic, and black pepper, then let it sit at least 30 minutes while you prep everything else.
Slice the onions into rings. Fry them in a little of the oil over medium heat until soft and just starting to brown, then pull them out and set them aside.
Lift the beef out of the marinade and save every drop of that liquid. Sear the beef in batches over high heat so it browns instead of steaming.
Return all the beef to the pot, pour in the reserved marinade and a splash of water, and bring it to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened into a glaze.
Cook the rice separately while the beef simmers.
Stir the fried onions back in for the last 2 minutes, taste, and add salt only if the soy sauce did not carry it far enough.

name: Braised Pork Ragu over Pappardelle
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Cut the pork loin into 2-inch chunks and season with salt and pepper. Heat the vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high and sear the pork in batches until browned on a couple of sides. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the diced onion, carrots, and celery for 5 to 6 minutes until softened, then add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 minute.
Pour in the beef broth and diced tomatoes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the thyme and Italian seasoning, then return the pork and its juices.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and braise on low heat (or in a 300F oven) for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the pork shreds easily with a fork.
Shred the pork right in the pot with two forks and simmer uncovered 10 to 15 minutes to thicken the sauce. Taste for salt.
Boil the fettuccine in salted water to al dente, drain, and fold it into the ragu until every ribbon is coated.

name: Bratwurst and Sauerkraut with Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F and grease two large baking dishes or deep sheet pans.
Cut the potatoes into even chunks and spread them across the pans, then season them with salt and black pepper.
Drain the sauerkraut, squeeze out some of the liquid, and scatter it over the potatoes.
Lay the bratwurst on top so they sit above the kraut and can brown instead of steam.
Pour the beef broth around the edges of the pans, then cover them tightly with foil.
Bake covered until the potatoes are tender all the way through, then pull the foil off and bake again until the brats are browned and split.
Slice the brats into thick coins and combine everything with the pan juices in your big pot.

name: Brazilian Feijoada Pork and Black Bean Stew Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 3 cans (794 g)
Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.75 lb (298 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the chopped bacon in a skillet, then use that fat to sear the cubed pork shoulder and the cubed beef chuck roast on all sides. Do it in batches so the meat browns instead of steams.
Cook the diced onion and minced garlic in the same skillet until soft, scraping up everything stuck to the bottom.

Move the bacon, seared meats, onion and garlic to the slow cooker along with the diced ham, the drained black beans, the chicken broth, the white vinegar, the bay leaves, ground coriander, salt and black pepper.
Cook on low for 8 to 9 hours, until the pork shreds under a fork and the beans have gone soft enough to thicken the liquid.
Mash a scoop of the beans against the side of the crock and stir it back in. That is what turns the broth into gravy.
Pull out the bay leaves, shred the larger pieces of meat, and cook the rice per the package to serve underneath.

name: Brazilian Galinhada (Chicken and Saffron Rice)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces and season them with salt, black pepper and the lemon juice. Let them sit 20 minutes while you chop everything else.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high and brown the chicken in batches until it has real color on both sides. Do not rush this, because the fond on the bottom of the pot is the entire flavor base. Set the chicken aside.
Cook the diced onion and green bell pepper in the same pot for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and the tomato paste and cook 2 more minutes until the paste turns brick red.
Stir in the dry rice and toast it for 2 minutes so every grain gets coated in the tomato and the drippings.
Add the diced tomatoes, chicken broth and bay leaves, then nestle the chicken back in with all its juices and bring the pot to a boil.
Drop to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 20 to 25 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and the chicken reads 165F.
Scatter the frozen peas over the top, re-cover, and let it sit off the heat 10 minutes. Then pull the bay leaves, fluff from the bottom, and fold in the sliced green onions.

name: Brazilian-Style Pork Ribs Bowls
ingredients: Apple Cider Vinegar (Great Value): 7.5 tbsp (112 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the marinade: minced garlic, grated onion, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, apple cider vinegar, honey, salt, pepper, oregano, cumin, and cayenne.
Cut the pork loin into thick slabs (about 1.5 inches), coat them in the marinade, and refrigerate at least 2 hours, overnight if you can plan that far ahead.
Preheat the oven to 375F. Arrange the pork in a roasting pan, pour any extra marinade over, and cover tightly with foil.
Roast covered for 35 to 40 minutes, then uncover, spoon the pan juices back over the meat, and roast 15 to 20 minutes more until the edges brown and the pork reaches at least 145F.
Rest the pork 10 minutes, then slice or cube it and toss it back through the pan juices.
While the pork roasts, cook 6.25 cups dry rice with water per package directions.
Combine the rice, pork, and every drop of pan sauce in your weighed pot.

name: Buffalo Chicken Pasta Bake
ingredients: Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 35 oz dry (992 g)
1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 21 oz (595 g)
Ranch Seasoning Mix (Hidden Valley): 3.5 tbsp (24 g)
Buffalo Wing Sauce (Frank's RedHot): 0.75 cups (214 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 2.25 lb (980 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 10.5 oz (297 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Preheat the oven to 375F. Cube the chicken breast, season with salt and pepper, and cook it in a skillet over medium-high until it reaches 165F. Set aside.
Boil the ziti in salted water until 2 minutes shy of al dente, then drain.
In your largest pot, melt the butter over medium heat, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Whisk in the cream cheese until smooth, then the ranch seasoning and buffalo wing sauce.
Fold in the cooked chicken and ziti until everything is coated, then spread into two 9x13 pans.
Top with the mozzarella and bake 15 to 20 minutes until melted and bubbling at the edges. Rest 5 to 10 minutes before combining into your weighed pot.

name: Buffalo Turkey and Potato Bowls
ingredients: Buffalo Wing Sauce (Frank's RedHot): 1 bottle (210 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (200 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): 1 tsp ground (8 g)
steps: Brown 6 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with a chopped yellow onion until no pink is left.
Bake the fries on sheet pans while the turkey cooks so nothing sits waiting.
Stir the buffalo wing sauce and shredded carrots into the turkey and let it simmer a few minutes.
Pile the buffalo turkey over the fries in each container.
Sprinkle the fat-free cheddar on top while everything is hot so it melts in.

name: Cajun Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 2.25 lb (1058 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat some of the olive oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high. Brown the sliced smoked sausage 3 to 4 minutes until the edges crisp, then set aside.
Add more oil and brown the chicken thigh chunks, seasoned with salt and pepper, until golden on the outside. They finish cooking in the rice.
Add the diced onions and cook 5 to 6 minutes until soft, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, chicken broth, Cajun seasoning, garlic powder, dried basil, parsley, and black pepper, then bring to a boil.
Add the dry rice, return the sausage and chicken, and stir once. Cover and simmer on low 22 to 25 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165F.
Rest off the heat, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff and taste for salt.

name: Cajun Chicken Etouffee Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Make the roux: heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium, whisk in the flour, and stir near-constantly for 10 to 15 minutes until it turns the color of peanut butter. Do not walk away; a burnt roux starts over.
Add the butter, diced onion, celery, and green bell pepper and cook 5 to 6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic for 1 minute more.
Gradually whisk in the chicken broth so the roux stays smooth, then add the Worcestershire, Cajun seasoning, thyme, bay leaves, and hot sauce.
Add the chicken thighs, cut into large bite-size pieces, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy thickens and the chicken reaches 165F. Pull the bay leaves and stir in most of the green onions.
Meanwhile, cook 3.75 cups dry rice with water per package directions.
Combine the rice and etouffee in your weighed pot, or portion rice first and ladle the etouffee over, your call. Finish with the remaining green onions.

name: Cambodian Beef Lok Lak Rice Bowls
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.75 cups (189 g)
Sweet Soy Sauce (ABC (Kecap Manis)): 1.25 oz (37 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Firm the beef in the freezer for about thirty minutes, then slice it thin against the grain.

Toss the beef with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sweet soy sauce, garlic, sugar, a pinch of baking soda, the all-purpose flour, and a heavy hand of freshly ground black pepper, and let it sit at least twenty minutes.
Cook the rice according to the package while the beef marinates.
Slice the red onions and cut the drained tomatoes into wedges, then set them aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet until it is smoking, and sear the beef in batches in a single layer, shaking the pan, until browned outside and barely done inside.
Return all the beef to the pan with any marinade left in the bowl and let it bubble down into a glaze for about a minute.
Kill the heat, add the lime juice, more black pepper, and salt to taste, and toss the red onion and tomato through so they warm without cooking.

name: Cantonese Beef, Tomato and Egg over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, then scramble them in some of the vegetable oil over medium heat until just barely set and still soft. Pull them out early, since they will finish in the sauce.
Stir the cornstarch into a little cold water to make a smooth slurry and set it aside.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan and cook the ground beef with the garlic powder until browned with no pink remaining.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook them down until they collapse and the sauce turns thick and glossy.
Stir in the ketchup, sugar, soy sauce, and chicken broth and simmer for a few minutes so the flavors settle.
Pour in the cornstarch slurry while stirring and cook until the sauce thickens and turns shiny.
Fold the scrambled eggs back in gently so they stay in soft curds, and season with salt and black pepper to taste.

name: Cantonese Turkey Rice Bowls
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 0.75 cups (189 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide skillet over medium-high, add the ground turkey, and brown it, breaking it into fine crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the diced onion and minced garlic and cook 4 minutes until the onion softens and goes translucent.
Pour in the chicken broth, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and black pepper, and bring it to a simmer for 5 minutes so the flavors settle in together.
Whisk the cornstarch with a half cup of cold water until smooth. Cold water, always, since cornstarch in hot liquid turns into lumps you cannot whisk out.
Stir the slurry into the simmering pan and cook 2 minutes until the sauce turns glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Add the frozen peas and the sesame oil and cook 2 minutes more, just until the peas are hot and still bright green.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the gravy in its own pan for portioning.
